text: King Nebuchadnezzar made an image of gold, ninety feet high and nine feet wide, and set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.
He sent word to gather the satraps, prefects, governors, advisers, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the provincial officials to come to the dedication of the image he had set up.
So they assembled and stood before the image Nebuchadnezzar had erected.
A herald called out loudly, "People of every nation and language, you are commanded:
as soon as you hear the sound of the horn, pipe, zither, lyre, harp, and every kind of music, you are to fall down and worship the golden image King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
Whoever does not fall down and worship will immediately be thrown into a blazing furnace."
So as soon as they heard the music, all the peoples fell down and worshiped the golden image King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
At that time some Chaldeans came forward and brought malicious charges against the Jews.
They said to King Nebuchadnezzar, "O king, live forever!
You have decreed, O king, that everyone who hears the music must fall down and worship the golden image,
and that whoever does not fall down and worship will be thrown into a blazing furnace.

But there are Jews you have put in charge of the province of Babylon — Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego — who pay no attention to you, O king. They do not serve your gods or worship the golden image you set up."
Furious with rage, Nebuchadnezzar summoned Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, and they were brought before the king.
Nebuchadnezzar said to them, "Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, that you do not serve my gods or worship the golden image I have set up?

Now, if you are ready, when you hear the music, to fall down and worship the image I made, very well. But if you refuse, you will immediately be thrown into a blazing furnace — and what god will be able to rescue you from my power?"
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego answered the king, "Nebuchadnezzar, we have no need to defend ourselves to you in this matter.
If we are thrown in, the God we serve is able to save us from the blazing furnace, and he will rescue us from your power, O king.
But even if he does not, we want you to know, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden image you have set up."
Then Nebuchadnezzar was filled with fury, and his expression changed against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego; he ordered the furnace heated seven times hotter than usual.
He commanded some of the strongest soldiers in his army to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and throw them into the blazing furnace.
So the men were bound in their robes, trousers, turbans, and other clothing, and thrown into the blazing furnace.
Because the king's order was so urgent and the furnace so extremely hot, the flames killed the soldiers who carried Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego up to it.
And these three men, firmly bound, fell into the blazing furnace.
Then King Nebuchadnezzar leaped up in amazement and asked his advisers, "Didn't we throw three men, bound, into the fire?" They replied, "Certainly, O king."
He said, "Look! I see four men, unbound, walking around in the fire unharmed — and the fourth looks like a son of the gods."

Nebuchadnezzar approached the opening of the blazing furnace and shouted, "Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out! Come here!" So Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego stepped out of the fire.

The satraps, prefects, governors, and royal advisers crowded around and saw that the fire had not harmed their bodies at all — not a hair of their heads was singed, their robes were unaffected, and there was no smell of smoke on them.

Nebuchadnezzar said, "Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who sent his angel and rescued his servants who trusted in him. They defied the king's command and gave up their lives rather than serve or worship any god except their own God.

Therefore I decree that anyone of any people, nation, or language who says anything against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego will be torn limb from limb and their houses turned to rubble, for no other god can rescue this way."
Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the province of Babylon.
